title: Private Console: Seamless Cluster Staging & Rollout Telemetry Ribbon
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Design and prototype a compact telemetry ribbon for Private Console cluster staging and rollout flows. The ribbon sits at the top of cluster detail and rollout screens and summarizes staging status, last upgrade, risk score, active canaries, and quick actions (pause/rollback/force-promote). Goal: surface actionable signals for on-call and platform owners without forcing deep-navigation into logs or charts. Build a visuals-first component plus keyboard-accessible quick-actions and an accessible color palette that can degrade to text-only for low-bandwidth/air-gapped deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Ribbon component implemented in Figma with tokenized states (ok/warning/critical/info)
Prototype demonstrates keyboard nav and action confirm flows (pause/rollback/promote)
Design handoff includes responsive variants for compact and expanded cluster pages
UX copy for status badges and hover tooltips reviewed by PM and Security
Integration checklist for engineering: data fields, telemetry endpoints, SLO links, and feature flags
links: ENG-2142 (backend): rollout state API and last-run summary
comments: 2026-01-27 — Sofia Martinez: Initial concept sketches posted. Focus on reducing clicks for common ops (pause/rollback/promote).
2026-02-02 — Rajat Mehra (Eng): Backend can expose a summary endpoint but needs a stable contract for 'riskScore' and 'canaryCount' — suggested adding a 30s TTL cache for cost reasons.
2026-02-06 — Lena Park: Iterated on compact variant to avoid pushing down important logs; added keyboard shortcuts and a confirmation micro-modal pattern.
2026-02-10 — Security review requested: need to confirm RBAC gating on quick-actions and audit logging for force-promote/rollback.
2026-02-15 — PM review: Suggested adding per-tenant cost exposure metric to ribbon for Dedicated customers. Added as optional chip.
2026-02-18 — Design review notes: reduce color reliance; include pattern for monochrome deployments and include explicit text fallback for status.
tradeoffs: High signal density vs discoverability: We prioritize surface-level actions but will hide destructive ops behind confirm flows to avoid accidental state changes.
Telemetry freshness vs cost: 30s TTL recommended to balance API cost with operational freshness; teams can toggle to live-stream for debugging.
Visual compactness vs accessibility: Provide expanded variant and text-only fallback to serve air-gapped / high-contrast needs.
